judgments.label: true_positive
judgments.rationale: The element is the photo in the 'Healthier aging' spotlight card, an illustration of a cell. It is the only content of its own link, which points to the news.mit.edu story 'unmasking zombie cells in aging tissue'. Its alt, 'colorful cell', describes how the picture looks, but the image is a functional image, a control. 1.1.1 asks a control's name to describe its purpose, and H30 asks an image link's alt to describe the destination. A keyboard or screen-reader user meets 'colorful cell, link' as a separate tab stop, with nothing saying it opens the 'Healthier aging' story. The 'Healthier aging' heading link that follows goes to the same URL but is a separate link, not combined with the image as in H2, so it does not give the image link a name. The live page on 2026-10-09 is unchanged. Some auditors would put the redundant link under 2.4.4 instead, but the finding's claim, that the alt is all the link holds and does not say where it leads, is a fair statement of a 1.1.1 failure for a functional image.
